issues.description: Redundant NewRateLimit+NewStats call leaks a counter under the old key on every override request
issues.detail: In the value_to_metric override block, NewRateLimit is invoked with statsManager.NewStats(rateLimit.FullKey) and then Stats is immediately overwritten with NewStats(enhancedKey). The first NewStats registers a counter under the old key that is never used, polluting the stats registry on a hot path. Drop the NewRateLimit recreate and just assign Stats and FullKey directly.

issues.description: Enhanced key builder appends segments past matched depth, producing divergent keys even when no flag is set
issues.detail: valueToMetricFullKey runs unconditionally for every entry, including when nextDescriptor is nil, writing entry.Key as a fallback. This causes enhancedKey to diverge from FullKey on partial matches and forces the override block to fire with a fabricated tail. Gate the override on an actual valueToMetric=true descriptor in the chain, and stop appending once matching ends.

issues.description: Three near-identical key-building branches should collapse into one decision
issues.detail: The matchedViaWildcard, matchedUsingValue, and default-key branches all reduce to: if (matchedUsingValue || (nextDescriptor.valueToMetric && entry.Value != "")) emit key_value else emit key. The three-way split is incidental complexity from carrying match-provenance flags that do not affect output. Collapse to one branch; the current expansion obscures the invariant and invites divergence on future edits.

issues.description: Metric-key construction complects descriptor lookup and two key builders inside one 80-line loop
issues.detail: GetLimit interleaves descriptor traversal, detailed_metric key building, and value_to_metric key building, with matchedViaWildcard and matchedUsingValue flags threaded between them. A pure buildMetricKey function over a recorded match-trace would decompose cleanly. Without that separation, every future metric variant adds another branch to the same loop, and the missing loop invariant makes the current logic hard to verify.

issues.description: Builder runs unconditionally on every GetLimit even when no descriptor uses value_to_metric
issues.detail: valueToMetricFullKey performs string allocation and comparison per entry on every call, regardless of whether the new flag is ever used in the config. Track a bool during traversal indicating any descriptor on the path has valueToMetric=true and skip the builder otherwise. This avoids charging existing users for an opt-in feature on the hot path.

issues.description: rateLimitDescriptor constructed by positional struct literal, fragile to future field additions
issues.detail: newDescriptor := &rateLimitDescriptor{map[...]{}, rateLimit, nil, descriptorConfig.ValueToMetric} uses positional initialization at two call sites edited in lockstep. The next person to add a field will silently shift meanings or have to touch every site. Use named field initialization for long-term maintainability.

synthesis.summary: The panel agrees the feature solves a real problem but the implementation has correctness, taste, and performance issues. The clearest P0s are a wasted NewStats call that leaks counters into the registry on every override request, and a key builder that appends segments past matched depth so enhancedKey can diverge from FullKey even when no value_to_metric flag is set. The three-branch key construction collapses to a single decision once the invariant is written down, and the whole builder should be gated on actual flag usage to avoid taxing existing users. Refactor the key builder into a pure function, drop the redundant NewRateLimit, gate the override on real flag presence, and switch struct literals to named fields.
